newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BUX ends lower on Dow, slow home market.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BUX ends lower on Dow, slow home market.

text.p: Hungarian share prices closed lower but above the day's lows on Friday weighed on by the Dow's two percent drop on Thursday and received only domestic impetus as the outside world was on holiday, traders said.
The BUX index closed at 5,413.70 points, down 25.27. BUX futures firmed for all maturities by between 50.00 and 117.50 points. June BUX closed at 5,840.50 points, up 55.50.

"A price slide bottomed out at about a 1.5 percent drop of the index but at that level some buyers appeared and there were some arbitrageurs as well and prices recovered as a result," said Gyorgy Czipo of ING Barings.

Friday's trend, however, could give hardly any hints on how trading will resume on Tuesday, he said, but if international sentiment remains subdued it could have a negative impact on the Hungarian market, too, he added.
"One cannot draw far-reaching consequences from today's session but if a downward international trend continues...we'll join that," Czipo said.
On Friday, MOL shares put on 60 forints or two percent to close at 3,060 forints after the oil company announced it had purchased Amoco Oil Holding Company 's Romanian retail operations.
Despite a higher close, MOL's market was volatile with its price moving between 2,970 and 3,065 forints.
Elsewhere on the market, meat processor Pick which may begin to produce mineral water after discovering a source on its company premises, closed at 11,560 forints, down 90.
Chemicals Borsodchem, whose management will propose to pay a 12 percent dividend on its 1996 results in addition to a 10 percent dividend advance, closed at 6,520 forints, down 10.
Pharmaceuticals Richter which plans to pay a 16 percent dividend against a 10 percent dividend last year on the ordinary stocks, finished at 11,350 forints, down 50.
Egis, which plans an unchanged eight percent dividend, dipped five forints to finish at 10,895.
